text:
marta: Customer hit partial websocket/chat frames — client gets an initial chunk (usually first token(s)), then ~10-30s pause, then the rest. They see no error on the client. Reported on iOS and a Node backend. Request-id: rq_8b3f1a. Happening on route /v1/streams via wss. Please gather repro steps + debug bundle.

devon: Can you get: request-id (you posted), exact model, region, whether they go through Cloudflare/ALB, and a short wscat or node repro? Also server logs for rq_8b3f1a with timestamped events (recv, start-gen, first-token, end).

marta: From customer: model=redwood-7b-instruct, region=us-west-2, edge=Cloudflare. They tried reconnecting; sometimes resumed chunk includes buffered tokens. They attached a tiny client snippet (Node fetch) that reproduces it for them: 

```js
// client-stream-repro.js (customer)
const WebSocket = require('ws');
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-7b-instruct', {
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <REDACTED>', 'X-Request-ID': 'rq_8b3f1a' }
});
ws.on('message', (data) => {
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), 'frame', data.toString().slice(0,80));
});
ws.on('open', () => console.log('open'))
ws.on('close', () => console.log('close'))
```

marta: Customer also tried wscat: `wscat -c \"wss://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-7b-instruct\" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'` — they see the same stop/start behaviour.

devon: Ok. Two common culprits: (1) client-side buffering (node, browser) — e.g., missing streaming handling or console buffering; (2) edge/proxy buffering (Cloudflare/ALB) coalescing frames during TCP/TLS-level timeouts. We should ask them to run these repros so we can compare timing:

1) Node frame logger (they already have above) but add timestamps on low-level socket events: add `ws._socket.on('data', ...)` to log raw TCP arrival times.
2) Try bypassing Cloudflare by targeting the regional control-plane endpoint (e.g., `us-west-2.api.redwood.com`) so we can see if the edge is the factor.
3) Capture a pcap for the session (tcpdump -w).

devon: To help customer run a quick curl SSE probe (if they can try SSE instead of ws) — this often shows chunk timing too: 

```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=redwood-7b-instruct \\
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

devon: Note the `-N` flag disables curl buffering so you see chunks as they arrive. Ask them to run both the ws and SSE repro and paste raw stdout.

ingrid: Oncall: If they can provide server logs for rq_8b3f1a, we want these fields (as separate lines if possible): `ts event detail` where event is e.g. `recv_request`, `start_infer`, `first_token_sent`, `stream_end`. If server shows tokens streaming out continuously but client pauses, it's client/edge. If server pauses in between, it's internal.

ingrid: Also request a HAR (for browser clients) or a Node `--trace` network log, and a pcap of the session: `sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.com and port 443 -w rq_8b3f1a.pcap`. They can redact payloads — we only need timing + sizes.

marta: Customer ran the simple Node script and attached logs (trimmed) and a pcap link: https://support.internal/tickets/5483/artifacts/rq_8b3f1a.pcap (sensitive token removed). Their stdout shows: 

```
2026-03-05T18:12:01.123Z open
2026-03-05T18:12:01.456Z frame \"Hello\"
2026-03-05T18:12:11.789Z frame \"\"
2026-03-05T18:12:41.900Z frame \" world! rest of generation\"
```

marta: They say the blank frame line is actually a long pause with no bytes — the pcap shows TLS records arriving but very small (TLS 10-20B) during the pause.

devon: Interesting — small TLS records often indicate Nagle or edge keepalive/coalescing. Ask them to test: 

- Bypass Cloudflare (regional endpoint)
- Re-run with TCP_NODELAY on their client (for Node: `ws._socket.setNoDelay(true)`)
- Re-run with `--no-compress` / disable per-message-deflate if enabled

devon: Also ask them to re-run the node repro with this modified snippet to log raw socket chunks: 

```js
ws._socket.on('data', (buf) => {
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), 'tcp', buf.length);
});
```

support-bot: debug-bundle created: db_rq_8b3f1a (contains pcap, client logs, server log export request queued).

marta: I'll ask the customer to run the `setNoDelay` test and to try the regional endpoint. I'll upload the node stdout + pcap to the ticket once they confirm. Thanks. :pray:

devon: Perfect. If they can't bypass edge, ask them to run a short repro with `curl -N` SSE and we can correlate server-side timestamps to the pcap. Also include which SDK version / ws library version.

marta: Will do. I'll follow up in ticket 5483 and paste the outputs here when available.
